messages:
IncidentBot: [ALERT] realtime-p99-latency > 3s for route `/v1/generate` (prod, us-west-2). Paging on-call: @Tara :rotating_light:
Tara: saw the page, joining. first check: is this systemic or single-model?
Jason: I'm seeing concurrent increases across model-gen-prod and model-gen-quant. p95 jumped from ~110ms to ~720ms, p99 from ~420ms to ~3.2s in the last 3m.
Priya: infra graphs show host GPU utilization is normal (~65%). No autoscaler events. No recent infra deploys in the last hour.
Neha: dashboard link: https://observability.redwood/boards/latency?range=5m - slow tail appears correlated with streaming requests (chunked responses) increasing in duration.
Tara: good call. streaming stalls usually point to runtime KV cache pressure or network stalls. Jason, can you check runtime logs for stall traces and gRPC backpressure?
Jason: grabbing logs. quick grep: `grep -n "stall" /var/log/runtime/*.log` shows repeated `kv-cache-miss` followed by `evicting-kv` around 1778881180.
Dino: customer support flags: 3 high-priority customers reported UI hangs. (tickets 4820, 4821, 4822)
Emily: customer impact looks real. Estimate 2% of traffic affected from sampling. Need mitigation ASAP.
Tara: immediate mitigations: 1) route streaming traffic to regular (non-streaming) endpoint fallback, 2) enable degraded mode (shorter max_tokens + disable prefix caching) for heavy routes, 3) temporarily widen routing to standby model variant. I'll coordinate.
Priya: I can add a routing rule: send requests with header `x-streaming: true` to fallback pool `gen-standby-2` with `fast-fallback=true`. Pushing now.
IncidentBot: deploy-bot: successfully updated route rule in 12s.
Jason: applying runtime flags to reduce KV cache churn: `RUNTIME_KV_CACHE_MAX=20000` -> `12000` and lowering `kv_evict_threshold` to 0.6. Rolling to 30% first.
Neha: after the first 30% rollout p95 -> 210ms, p99 -> 1.1s. Good signal.
Tara: keep rolling. Priya, can you spin an extra pool of smaller instances for streaming fallback? Not autoscaled — manual add to avoid overshoot.
Priya: launching 6 x g4dn.xlarge in fallback pool. ETA ~90s.
Jason: logs show some long tails still stuck at the runtime network layer: `grpc: transport: connection is closing` followed by `requeue request`. Might be transient connection churn with streaming keep-alives.
Dino: support messages: customers seeing partial responses then long wait. We posted a status note to the dashboard: "Investigating increased latency for streaming responses" :information_source:
Emily: good. let's mark SLO blip and track impact for SLA reporting. I'll start a ticket.
Tara: checklist for next 10m: 1) complete runtime rollout, 2) confirm fallback routing holds traffic, 3) monitor p95/p99 and streaming error rates, 4) tag affected traces for postmortem.
Neha: metrics after rollout to 70%: p95=180ms, p99=420ms, streaming error-rate down 3x. Dashboard: https://observability.redwood/boards/latency?range=10m
Jason: finished rollout to 100% with adjusted cache knobs. No errors in canary.
Priya: fallback pool up and accepting connections. routing shows ~14% of streaming requests shifted.
Tara: lowering alert sensitivity to watch-only for 10m. If values creep back, we re-open paging.
IncidentBot: Alert update: p99 now 430ms (was 3.2s). Severity: reduced.
Dino: customers acknowledged the status update, some still waiting for full recovery but fewer timeouts.
Emily: action items for postmortem: - correlate kv-cache eviction spikes with request patterns - evaluate streaming keep-alive behavior - consider graceful draining for streaming connections during runtime rolling updates - playbook update to include streaming->fallback rule
Jason: saving logs and flamegraphs to S3: `s3://redwood-incidents/1778881234/`
Neha: tagging traces: `tag:latency-1778881234` on 1200 traces.
Tara: handing off to Priya and Jason for follow-up over next 8 hours. I'll be available for major regressions, but moving back to watch.
Priya: ack. I'll keep autoscaler and pool dashboards open.
Jason: ack, will dig into root cause next (likely KV eviction pattern + streaming connection churn).
Dino: I'll follow up with the three impacted customers with timeline and next steps.
Emily: thanks team. Drafting initial incident summary for ops shortly.
Tara: closing active page, leaving the thread open for writeup and RCA items. :white_check_mark:
